# 🧠 Handwritten Digit Recognizer (CNN + Streamlit)

A deep learning project that predicts handwritten digits (0–9) using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on the EMNIST dataset, enhanced with synthetic data for better real-world performance.

---

## 🚀 Features

- 🔢 Digit classification (0–9)
- 🧠 CNN model built with PyTorch
- 🎨 Streamlit web app for image upload
- 🧪 Advanced preprocessing pipeline
- 📊 Confidence score + probability distribution
- 🔝 Top-3 predictions
- ⚡ Works with real handwritten images (not just MNIST)

---
## 🧠 Model Details

- Architecture: CNN (Conv → ReLU → BatchNorm → FC)
- Input: 28x28 grayscale image
- Output: 10 classes (digits 0–9)
- Loss: CrossEntropyLoss
- Optimizer: Adam

---

## 📊 Dataset

- **EMNIST (digits split)** — base dataset
- **Synthetic dataset (OpenCV generated)** — improves generalization

---

## 🧪 Preprocessing Pipeline

- Grayscale conversion
- Contrast normalization
- Noise reduction (Gaussian blur)
- Adaptive thresholding
- Contour detection & cropping
- Centering in 28×28 canvas
- Normalization to match training distribution

---
🎨 Run Web App
streamlit run app.py

# Model Summary

AxiaLM 1-7M is an (intentionally) absolutely tiny model. It's meant to run on cheap hardware locally. However, this comes at a cost, it is probably almost nowhere near able to hold a full conversation, it's just able to hold good consistent grammar — actually I take that back, it CAN hold a conversation, but it'll be talking to itself, not you.

## Usage

This model can be used on ridiculously limited hardware, even school issued chromebook with 4GB of RAM. I wouldn't really recommend using it for any other purposes.

## System

This model is a standalone.

## Implementation requirements

Two T4 Tesla GPUs were used to fully train this model from scratch in about ~2 hours.

# Model Characteristics

It's very dumb.

## Model initialization

It was trained from scratch, as said before.

## Model stats

AxiaLM 1-7M has 7,000,000 parameters, Transformers, SwiGLU, and RMSNorm.

## Other details

The model comes with FP32 and INT8.

## Data Overview + Training Dataa

It was pre-trained on WikiText-103 + BookCorpus. It was conversationally fine-tuned on BlendedSkillTalk + Alpaca-cleaned + OpenHermes + WizardLM-Evol.

## Demographic groups

Not much.

## Evaluation data

Nope.

It tried. Badly.

## Summary

idonthaveevaluationresults.idk

## Subgroup evaluation results

No.

## Fairness 

?

## Usage limitations

Literally everything.

## Ethics

Nope. It can't do jack diggity squat.

# 📱 TFLite SMS Spam Classifier (On-Device NLP Model)

## 🚀 Overview
This project provides a lightweight **SMS Spam Detection model** built using TensorFlow and optimized with TensorFlow Lite (TFLite) for **real-time, on-device inference**.

The model is designed to classify incoming SMS messages into:
- Spam
- Not Spam (Ham)

It is optimized for **mobile applications (Android / Flutter)** and works fully offline without requiring any server communication.

---

## 🎯 Key Features
- ✅ Fully on-device inference (No Internet required)
- ⚡ Fast prediction using TensorFlow Lite
- 📦 Lightweight model (optimized for mobile)
- 🔒 Privacy-friendly (no data leaves device)
- 📱 Easily integrable with Flutter apps

---

## 🧠 Model Details
- Model Type: Text Classification (Binary)
- Framework: TensorFlow → TensorFlow Lite
- Input: SMS text (string)
- Output: Probability scores

Example Output:
[Spam: 0.92, Ham: 0.08]

---

## 📥 Input Format
- Raw SMS text string

Example:
"Congratulations! You have won a free lottery ticket. Call now!"

---

## 📤 Output Format
- Probability array:
  - Index 0 → Spam probability
  - Index 1 → Ham (Not Spam) probability

---

## 🏗️ Model Architecture (Typical)
- Text preprocessing (tokenization / vectorization)
- Embedding layer
- Dense layers
- Sigmoid / Softmax output

---

## 📦 Files Included
- model.tflite → Optimized TFLite model
- labels.txt → Class labels
- README.md → Documentation

---

## ⚙️ Usage (Python - TFLite Inference)

```python
import tensorflow as tf

interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_path="model.tflite")
interpreter.allocate_tensors()

input_details = interpreter.get_input_details()
output_details = interpreter.get_output_details()

# Example input (preprocessed)
input_data = ...

interpreter.set_tensor(input_details[0]['index'], input_data)
interpreter.invoke()

output_data = interpreter.get_tensor(output_details[0]['index'])
print(output_data)
